issue_context.title: Application Crashes when I turn on "Enable Dual Pane View"
issue_context.body:
I was discovering the settings of the Files app and when I turn on "Enable Dual Pane View" option, App Crashes unexpectedly. This happens only when turning it on, this does not happen when I turn it off.

**To reproduce**
1. Go to Settings of Files
2. Choose Multitasking
3. From the Dual Pane section turn on Enable Dual Pane View.
Remember: this only happens while turning it on. This does not happen when you turn it off.

It should not crash when I turn it on. When it crashed, I got a notification from the Files app. So, I am here to report.

**Logfile**
[debug.txt](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/6216778/debug.txt)
[debug_fulltrust.txt](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/6216779/debug_fulltrust.txt)

**Screenshots**
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61900781/112741021-8cd1d300-8fa1-11eb-9b53-25ef54f5e66f.mp4

**System Information**
 - OS Version: 
   Edition	Windows 10 Pro Insider Preview
   Version	Dev
   Installed on	‎3/‎25/‎2021
   OS build	21343.1000
   Experience	Windows 10 Feature Experience Pack 321.7401.0.3

 - App version:: v1.5.2.0

**Additional comment**
Yes, it happens after restarting the app too.
comments: @binamracode This issue should be resolved with #4313.

review_comments: Should this view model be renamed to SidebarViewModel?
The view model contains most of the adaptive behavior for the sidebar which drove my naming decision. I don't think it's really that important as long as it contains the word sidebar in it.

@duke7553 Back to the times where we had a hard time naming things 😆. I think it's best to call it SidebarViewModel because adding adaptive to the name can sound like it's limited to the adaptive behavior.
I am not sure the toolbar should be accessing MainPage, what do you think?
@yaichenbaum Do you have any alternative?
Can we use a dependency property instead?
@yaichenbaum Where? Would it ever make sense to change this reference from where the control is used?
@duke7553 I don't think so, however, if we want to view this as a decoupled control, we shouldn't have the reference here.
@yaichenbaum I'm not aware of any alternative based on how things are designed.

For the record, we'll keep this reference until we move vertical tabs out of the control and into MainPage with a later PR. It's a temporary solution that we can't do any better with right now. Also, take a look at PaneHolderPage. I removed the reference from there completely.
Wouldn't that create a circular reference?

@d2dyno1 No, it wouldn't create one because the lines you referenced merely show exposing ActivePane to be an interface member. Anyways, circular references are not likely to be the cause of our memory use problem.

> No, it wouldn't create one because the lines you referenced merely show exposing ActivePane to be an interface member. 

`IPaneHolder` is a member of `IMultiPaneInfo` and `IShellPage` inherits from `IMultiPaneInfo` so the `IShellPage` is accessible.

@d2dyno1 It doesn't create a new circular reference. I only made the existing one accessible to the interface. Nothing new to see here because (like I just stated) circular references are likely not the cause of our memory leak issue.
